title: Teaching
text:
Lecturer, School of Statistics and Actuarial Sciences, University of the Witwatersrand, April 2018 – present.
My teaching spans undergraduate and postgraduate courses in applied statistics, spatial statistics, survival analysis, and statistical programming. I bring a strong commitment to bridging theory with practice, with R statistical software central to my pedagogy.

title: Teaching
text:
Teaching Philosophy
My teaching philosophy centres on fostering critical thinking, practical problem-solving, and a deep understanding of statistical concepts. I create engaging and inclusive learning environments where students feel empowered to explore and actively participate — integrating theory with real-world applications through R statistical software, R Shiny applications, live coding, and collaborative activities.
I tailor my approach to each audience: simplifying concepts for service courses without sacrificing depth, guiding applied students through both theory and software implementation, and introducing challenging problems for students with strong mathematical backgrounds.
Key innovations include:

R Studio Cloud for real-time feedback on student scripts during online learning
R Shiny applications for interactive exploration of statistical concepts without prior coding experience
Pre-semester R Bootcamp (2022 cohort) to address foundational gaps after online learning disruptions
Group-based R Shiny projects to promote applied, collaborative learning
Sentiment analysis of student qualitative feedback to gain deeper insight into learning experiences

title: Supervision
text: I supervise Honours and Masters students in statistics, with projects spanning infectious disease modelling, spatial statistics, and wastewater-based epidemiology. Several students have received national recognition through the South African Statistical Association (SASA) competitions.

title: Supervision
text:
Future Goals
I aim to recruit and mentor at least two additional Honours students and one Masters student by end of 2025, and to secure support for a PhD student by mid-2026. Annual research workshops for postgraduate students are planned from 2026, creating a collaborative environment for spatial analysis and computational methods training.

title: Join Us
text: I welcome motivated students and collaborators interested in spatial statistics, infectious disease modelling, and public health data science. My research group is based at the University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg.

title: Join Us
text:
Prospective Students
Honours Students — I supervise Honours projects annually in the School of Statistics and Actuarial Sciences. Projects typically focus on one of my core research themes: spatio-stochastic modelling, spatial epidemiology, wastewater surveillance, or tuberculosis modelling. Students with a strong foundation in statistics and an interest in R programming are especially encouraged to reach out.
Masters Students — I am open to supervising Masters students on topics aligned with my research programme. Interested students should contact me with a brief research statement and their academic transcript.
PhD Students — I am actively seeking funding to support a PhD student by mid-2026. If you are interested in pursuing a PhD in spatial epidemiology or statistical public health, please get in touch to discuss possibilities.

title: Research Funding
text:
About My Funding
My research has been funded through collaborative partnerships within SEPIMOD and through competitive applications to South African national funding bodies. My contributions have involved developing and applying innovative spatial and computational models, facilitating collaborative research efforts, and providing expertise in modelling and data analysis.
I am currently pursuing independent funding as Primary Investigator through the NRF Thuthuka programme, which would support a comprehensive research initiative focusing on developing statistical methods for spatially misaligned health data, enhancing spatial-temporal modelling for disease surveillance, and creating spatial optimisation tools for TB intervention strategies.

      Lecturer in Statistics at the University of the Witwatersrand, specialising in applied & spatial statistics, stochastic modelling, and survival analysis.
      Dr. Manjoo-Docrat develops computational methods for understanding infectious disease dynamics, with a focus on spatio-stochastic models that capture the spatially heterogeneous nature of epidemic spread. She completed a post-doctoral fellowship at Johns Hopkins University focused on modelling tuberculosis transmission.
      She is a founding member of SEPIMOD — the Spatial Epidemic Modelling Group — an interdisciplinary consortium advancing public health research across South Africa.

text:
Research

  47Citations
  4h-index
  2i10-index

  2018At Wits Since



  
    01
    Spatio-Stochastic Modelling of Infectious Disease Spread
    Developing spatial components integrated into discrete-time binomial chain models for nuanced understanding of disease transmission dynamics, including local transmission, inter-regional interactions, and migration between spatial units.
  
  
    02
    Spatial Epidemiology of COVID-19
    Spatially explicit SEIR models incorporating a vulnerability index reflecting socioeconomic and health-related disparities, alongside mobility data, illustrated using South African COVID-19 data to inform targeted public health responses.
  
  
    03
    Wastewater-Based Epidemiology (WBE)
    Exploring cost-effective community-level disease surveillance through wastewater analysis, developing spatial methods for early-warning systems and hotspot identification in urban and peri-urban settings.
  
  
    04
    Modelling Tuberculosis in Vulnerable Populations
    Individual-based models for TB prevalence in high-risk populations, incorporating COVID-19 disruptions and developing spatial optimisation tools for vaccination and resource allocation.
  
  
    05
    Innovative Approaches to Teaching R in Statistics
    Examining R programming integration into undergraduate and postgraduate curricula, evaluating pedagogical strategies, and developing open-source R packages for spatial epidemiological modelling.
